kata.name: Abstract-factory missing combination - (ModernFactory, table) has no Cell row at all; the kernel is silent and the cross-product totality remains an expressibility gap (null result)
kata.series_report: docs/ref/pattern-kata-dispositions.md row Abstract Factory (`disposed — construction only; no invariant on a finite instance`); fixtures/katas/abstract-factory/README.md (pre-registered); beads catherine-r5k.1
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered null result: the kernel's totality ranges over declared Cell rows, so a pair with no row cannot dangle; check emits nothing and the baseline sample omits the pair (killed)

expected.detail: ModernFactory has no Cell row for the declared kind table; every declared cell is filled and agrees, table is still witnessed by VictorianFactory/table, so check emits [] and the frozen sample omits the pair. The cross-product universal is not expressible: no new predicate/surface exists

commands: python3 prototype/abstract_factory_baseline.py --assert  # exit 0: both arms silent on the missing pair
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/abstract-factory/05-missing-combination.ct.json --json  # exit 0, findings []

comparison.conventional_baseline: the frozen five-pair sample omits ModernFactory/table and all three sampled kinds are realized (table via VictorianFactory), so the baseline detects nothing; the kernel also emits nothing.

baseline.artifact: prototype/abstract_factory_baseline.py sha256:4f635702ad371a9c1155965763f18e2fda0d8a6289455fb708fe60e2dcb07c97 (frozen per-fixture (factory, kind) sample; always executed before the probe arm)

expressibility_gap.invariant: every (concrete factory, declared product kind) pair is realized
expressibility_gap.why: the kernel evaluates declared Cell rows; a pair with no row has no cell to resolve, and no quantifier ranges over Factory x Kind. Expressing it would need a new totality/coverage surface (or authored rows for every pair, which is the same authoring gap). This is the named missing law: declared-grid totality is executable, cross-product totality is not

expressibility_gap.invariant: functor composition (Abstract Factory as a functor: F(g o f) = F(g) o F(f))
expressibility_gap.why: the model carries no product-operation arrows, so the dictionary's functor law has no truth value on this surface (G2)

discrepancies: A conventional test that enumerated the cross product would catch the missing pair; a sampled one misses it. Both arms are silent here, so the entry is a null result (killed), not a probe advantage and not parity-as-victory.
The orphan product ModernTable is also unreferenced; consistent with G4, not counted.
procedure: 1. The law (AF-T, declared-grid product-family totality) and the fault matrix were committed in fixtures/katas/abstract-factory/ before any recorded run (README.md, faults.json); the pre-registration sections are not edited after the run.

2. The baseline arm (prototype/abstract_factory_baseline.py, sha256 pinned in comparison.baseline.artifact) was executed first: a frozen per-fixture sample of (factory, kind) realization sites asserting exactly one declared Cell, a resolved product, kind agreement, family agreement, plus one coverage assertion per sampled kind. Sites outside the sample are never inspected.

3. The probe arm ran the same fixtures through the real CLI: `catherine check --json`. Witnesses were mapped to presentation elements cell:<Factory>/<Kind> (dangling on cell_product/cell_factory/cell_kind, equation violations on a Cell row, key collisions on the shared site) and kind:<Kind> (dangling on kind_witness).

4. unique_detections = executed probe elements minus baseline-identified elements. The constructed catalog is not consulted (the kata id is unregistered there, so expectations are the pre-registered rows in this record). A construction rejection is recorded but never counted.

5. Verdict follows the recorded rule: empty unique = killed; non-empty unique with an executed baseline arm = survived; a claim resting only on a hypothesis or construction probe would be inconclusive.
